comments.body:
RCA (rebar-debug, Phase 1 complete) — DISPOSITION: ESCALATE (design decision required; not auto-landed)

STEP 0 / ORIENT
- 0(a) tracker sweep: no duplicate. This ticket is the single tracker for the deferred run_sweep site. Sibling injurious-pugnacious-azurevase (c0f6, in_progress) covers a DIFFERENT set (str()/realpath()/abspath() variants), not this site.
- 0(b) reported-against floor: filed as a split-off from auspicial-friended-merganser (2ec7, Gerrit 2326, 98f21fbc). Suspect path src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py unchanged on origin/main since (verified).
- 0(c) worktree at origin/main 82a0d5cd328f (= origin/main).

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (dynamic, runtime-confirmed)
run_sweep(tracker) at src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:222 hardcodes repo_root = os.path.dirname(tracker) and passes it EXPLICITLY to compact.compact_all_cli([], repo_root=repo_root). compact_all_cli reads the [compact] config via config.compose_config(repo_root).compact (threshold, COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS). On a RELOCATED store (REBAR_TRACKER_DIR outside the checkout — the deployed MCP topology: store at /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets, code at /app) the store's parent has no rebar.toml, so the sweep reads DEFAULT compaction config (threshold=10, horizon=1800s) instead of the code-root config. tracker_dir stays correct (REBAR_TRACKER_DIR wins verbatim), so the sweep folds the RIGHT tickets by the WRONG rule. Impact is milder than the parent's gate-disable: no gate is silently turned off; a non-default [compact] config is ignored.

PROOF (discriminating experiment, runtime)
Relocated store (REBAR_TRACKER_DIR outside checkout), code-root rebar.toml sets [compact] threshold=1, COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS=0. Seeded a fresh 4-comment task.
- run_sweep(tracker): SNAPSHOT NOT written — read default threshold/horizon from dirname(tracker), folded nothing (RED).
- On the SAME store, compact_all_cli([], repo_root=<code root>) DID fold (SNAPSHOT written).
Only variable = repo_root (dirname(tracker) vs code root). Confirms repo_root resolution is the sole cause; rules out "events not foldable" / "store misresolved".

DEFECT LEGITIMACY: defect. The relocatable store is a SUPPORTED feature (EV-3b; tracker_dir_override; scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py). Same construct class as auspicial-friended-merganser (closed Fixed) and chuffy-arbored-goldfish (closed Fixed). This site is the ONE the AC#4 guard explicitly sanctions/defers.

DEFECT ORIGIN (caused_by): the run_sweep dirname(tracker) line was introduced by commit d2dea317ec94 ("Trigger compaction from the close, out of band"), rebar-ticket 1fde-becd-942a-4351 (gaudy-gangrenous-basilisk). git blame -L222,222 is unambiguous and non-carrier (that commit WROTE the line); the site was born wrong (never handled a relocated store), so class = plan_defect. NOTE / divergence from the whole-class default: the parent auspicial attributed to 65e3-1fc6-5f3b-4c67 (stab-bunch-foyer), which introduced the transition.py gate site — a DIFFERENT commit. Each site of the shared construct class was shipped by its own commit; this site's is 1fde. caused_by link recorded (6bf1 -> 1fde).

WHY ESCALATE (the deferred design decision is real, not stale)
AC#1 requires the detached-child path to receive a correct code root, and AC#3 requires ZERO sanctioned sites — so the sync path alone cannot close this. The blocker is genuine and specific: WHAT durable code root should the detached child receive?
- maybe_compact already HAS a resolved repo_root (transition_close: str(config.repo_root(repo_root))), and spawn_detached already supports threading extra argv strings (its docstring documents the optional-sentinel pattern) — so the mechanical plumbing exists.
- BUT the two supported topologies want DIFFERENT sources:
  * Deployment (truly relocated store, STABLE /app via REBAR_ROOT): the child should get maybe_compact's repo_root (=/app). Correct and durable.
  * Local `make worktree` (store co-located via a .tickets-tracker SYMLINK; EPHEMERAL worktree code root): transition_close's repo_root = git-toplevel-of-cwd = the ephemeral worktree, which dies with the worktree. Today _spawn_detached_sweep deliberately hands the child StorePaths(tracker).canonical, and dirname(canonical) = the DURABLE main checkout — which is CORRECT locally. Naively threading maybe_compact's repo_root would point the outliving child at a dying worktree (a re-run of the durability class of bugs 3198/93a9), degrading to default config after teardown.
There is no existing helper returning the right durable code root for BOTH topologies; reconciling them (argv vs env; spawning-repo-root vs canonical-store-parent; how to stay durable across worktree teardown) is a config-root-discovery / process-detachment SEMANTICS decision. That exceeds the behavior-preserving/localized bar auspicial's other 8 sites met, exactly as this ticket's description anticipated.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION
Treat as a small design ticket, not a mechanical mirror. Recommended design: give run_sweep an optional second argv param (spawn_detached sentinel ""), and have maybe_compact pass a DURABILITY-RESOLVED code root — REBAR_ROOT/explicit when set (covers the deployment), else fall back to dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical) (covers the local co-located-symlink worktree, preserving today's correct behavior). run_sweep threads it into compact_all_cli; then remove the # repo-root-ok: sanction (AC#3 -> zero allowlisted sites) and add the guard-clean assertion. RED->GREEN oracle: (1) the relocated-store fold proven RED above (sync path), (2) a _spawn_detached_sweep argv-threading unit assertion (mirrors test_a_detached_sweep_child_is_handed_the_canonical_store_tracker) for the detached path. This needs a human design sign-off on the durable-root resolution rule before implementation; per agent policy I am not landing it unilaterally.

SCOPE/CALLERS: run_sweep has exactly two callers — maybe_compact (sync trigger=always) and the detached child entry via spawn_detached (string ref). Blast radius is contained to compact_trigger.py + the spawn argv contract. No new dependency, no new capability.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 2344 (45dba2bb841b), pushed for review, NOT submitted.

SEQUENCING CHECK (mandatory precondition). injurious-pugnacious-azurevase (c0f6-0fc9-fe48-41bc) — the sibling that also declares scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py in its file impact — has LANDED on origin/main as 1049da8f61b8 ("Fix config root in composer save-time advisories"). Its guard extension (the str()-wrapped store argument) and its _store/sync.py sanctions are already merged; the ticket is merely not yet closed. So there was no concurrent editor of the guard and no sequencing conflict. This change edits only the guard's DOCSTRING (draining the run_sweep sanction from the "sanctioned sites today" list), which does not touch the detection logic c0f6 added. Note c0f6 also split the realpath()/abspath() family out to flowered-basaltic-beagle (088b-e4c1-050c-4516) — disjoint from this site, which is the bare dirname(tracker) form.

THE STALE BLOCKER, CORRECTED. This ticket's description and its RCA both concluded that a correct code root needed a spawn-contract change, on the premise that "there is no existing helper returning the right durable code root for BOTH topologies". That premise is false, and the description has been corrected so the next reader is not misled:
  * Deployment: REBAR_ROOT is exported UNCONDITIONALLY (infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:102 ENV; infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:294 documents that it is deliberately outside the PAT guard), so repo_root_or_none()'s second precedence arm resolves the code root directly.
  * Local worktree: _proc.detached_child_cwd (src/rebar/_proc.py:127-150) ALREADY anchors the detached child's cwd at dirname(realpath(tracker)) — the durable main checkout, with realpath load-bearing precisely to escape the ephemeral worktree's .tickets-tracker symlink (bugs 3198/93a9). So the git-toplevel arm lands on the durable code root, preserving today's correct local behaviour.
The RCA's own worry — "naively threading maybe_compact's repo_root would point the outliving child at a dying worktree" — is an argument AGAINST the spawn-contract design, not against resolution. The rejected alternative is recorded in the commit message: threading the root reimplements repo_root_or_none() at the spawn site, where the parent's root is the dying worktree.

THE FIX. One line in the child: `repo_root = config.repo_root_or_none()` at compact_trigger.py run_sweep, replacing `os.path.dirname(tracker)`; the `# repo-root-ok:` sanction is removed. snapshot_repo_root() was NOT used — its snapshot-specific "." fallback (_config_resolvers.py:444-462) is the fatherly-incoherent-mare outage shape and run_sweep does not want it. A stale comment at the _spawn_detached_sweep call site, which justified handing over the canonical tracker partly because "inside run_sweep this argument also becomes repo_root = dirname(tracker)", was corrected too — the canonical-tracker rationale stands on the cwd-durability ground alone.

TESTS (RED-first, mutation-checked). tests/unit/test_relocated_store_repo_root.py gains three: the sweep folds per the repo's non-default [compact] block on a relocated store; the root handed to compact_all_cli IS the resolved code root (pinned at the seam); and a repo config that folds nothing still folds nothing. Config comes from a rebar.toml FILE, never REBAR_COMPACT_THRESHOLD / REBAR_COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS, because an env read is root-independent and would hide the bug. tests/unit/test_repo_root_from_tracker_guard.py gains the AC#3 assertion that no config-root site is deferred behind a sanction.

Note on the contrast control: the first draft pivoted it on the threshold and was WRONG — select_tickets' BACKFILL arm selects any snapshot-less ticket with at least one foldable event whatever the threshold, so it folded anyway. The real discriminator is the HORIZON (the default 1800 s puts just-written events out of reach, which is exactly why the buggy root folded nothing). Rewritten to pivot on the horizon and documented in the test.

MUTATION RESULTS — 3 mutants, 3 killed.
  M1 re-seed the exact defect, dirname(tracker): BOTH behaviour tests fail. Killed.
  M2 drop the resolver and hand repo_root=None (let compose_config discover downstream): the FOLD test still PASSES — the outcome is accidentally right in-test — and only the seam assertion catches it. Killed by the seam test alone. This is the "a different guard rescues it" trap; without the seam test the mutant survives.
  M3 dirname(realpath(tracker)), the plausible near-miss: both fail. Killed.
Restored: green.

GATES (all local, worktree venv; no MCP agentic op): make lint PASS; make typecheck PASS (683 files); pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py 4 passed; scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check new=0 increased=0; scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py rc=0 with zero deferred config-root sites; the three touched unit modules 50 passed.

NOT CLOSED: change 2344 awaits LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Design rationale (moved out of the description to keep it under the plan-review admission limit)

**Why a dedicated resolver, not `config.repo_root_or_none()`.** `repo_root_or_none()` is explicit > `REBAR_ROOT` > git-toplevel-of-**cwd**. Its non-`REBAR_ROOT` fallback reads the child's CWD, so it only lands on the durable checkout if the child's cwd is anchored there — it leans on `detached_child_cwd` behaviour and re-runs the worktree-durability class (bugs 3198/93a9) if the cwd is a dying `make worktree` toplevel. The operator-approved `dirname(canonical tracker)` is durable independent of cwd: `StorePaths(tracker).canonical` realpath-resolves the worktree `.tickets-tracker` symlink back to the durable main checkout store, and its dirname is that checkout.

**Rejected alternatives.**
- Threading the caller's resolved `repo_root` from `maybe_compact` through the spawn contract — the parent's root is the DYING worktree; a `make worktree` git-toplevel can be deleted out from under the running detached child (durability class 3198/93a9).
- `config.repo_root_or_none()` — git-toplevel-of-cwd fallback, see above.
- `snapshot_repo_root()` — adds a snapshot-specific `"."` fallback `run_sweep` does not want; a code root that silently becomes cwd is the fatherly-incoherent-mare outage shape.

**Topology coverage.** Deployment (relocated store): `REBAR_ROOT` is exported unconditionally (`infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:102`; `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:294` places it outside the PAT guard) naming the provisioned checkout `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`, so the first precedence arm resolves it. Local `make worktree` (co-located symlink store, `REBAR_ROOT` may be unset): the fallback arm resolves via `dirname(canonical tracker)`.

**Scope boundaries.** Relates to ADR 0051 (foreground git maintenance never detached — this child does config resolution only). Does NOT overlap flowered-basaltic-beagle (088b-e4c1-050c-4516) realpath/abspath config-root family: this fix routes through `StorePaths.canonical`, not a raw realpath/abspath wrapper, so it adds no new per-site realpath decision of that kind.

**P2 note (review):** the plan-review advisory overlap flags `1a33-8b6a-5bf2-4ab6` also touches `src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py` (confidence 0.72). Left unlinked deliberately — my change only APPENDS a new leaf resolver and does not depend on 1a33's work; adding a `depends_on` would serialise unrelated tickets. Escalate if 1a33 turns out to edit the same region.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CONCURRENT-WORK COLLISION — read before implementing the current plan. Not resolving this unilaterally; flagging it for the operator.

WHAT LANDED. A change implementing this ticket is ALREADY MERGED on origin/main as c68cc1de3185 ("Resolve the sweep's code root, not compose it", Gerrit 2344, submitted by JoeOakhartNava at 22:56). It carries LLM-Review+1 and Verified+1 (CI run 33216372220 SUCCESS) and the rebar-ticket: 6bf1-326b-7404-4034 trailer. It implements run_sweep as the BARE `config.repo_root_or_none()`, removes the `# repo-root-ok:` sanction (guard allowlist now holds zero deferred config-root sites), and adds four tests to tests/unit/test_relocated_store_repo_root.py plus the guard self-test.

WHAT THE DESCRIPTION NOW SAYS. The description has since been rewritten to mandate a DIFFERENT design — a dedicated `compaction_child_repo_root(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)` with precedence REBAR_ROOT-realpath > dirname(canonical tracker) — and AC#1 explicitly excludes "`repo_root_or_none()` git-toplevel arm". That symbol does not exist anywhere in origin/main. So the current ACs describe work that is NOT what landed, which is why the close gate reports every box unchecked: I will not tick boxes for an implementation that is not in the tree, and per policy I will not --force.

THE DESIGN DISAGREEMENT, STATED FAIRLY. The rationale comment above is right that `repo_root_or_none()`'s non-REBAR_ROOT arm reads git-toplevel-of-CWD, so the merged implementation's local-topology correctness DEPENDS on `_proc.detached_child_cwd` continuing to anchor the child at dirname(realpath(tracker)). That is a real non-local coupling, and the merged code documents it explicitly rather than hiding it. It also applies unevenly: run_sweep has a SYNCHRONOUS caller too (maybe_compact when compact.trigger == "always"), where no anchoring applies and the cwd is simply the caller's.

But the proposed replacement is not strictly better, and the tradeoff should be made with eyes open: its fallback arm, `dirname(canonical tracker)`, IS "compose the config root from the store path" — the exact construct this ticket's whole class exists to eliminate and that scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py flags. It is correct only while REBAR_ROOT is set on every relocated store; a relocated store with REBAR_ROOT unset gets the store's parent, i.e. the original bug. So one design leans on cwd anchoring, the other leans on REBAR_ROOT always being exported. Both are defensible; neither is free.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION (operator decision, not mine).
(a) If the merged design is accepted: revert the description's AC block to describe what landed, tick the boxes, and close. No code change needed.
(b) If the dedicated resolver is preferred: keep this ticket open and land it as a follow-up REFACTOR on top of c68cc1de3185 — not as a from-scratch implementation, since the sanction is already drained and the tests already exist. Note that a `dirname(canonical tracker)` fallback will need its own `# repo-root-ok:` sanction or it re-populates the guard allowlist this ticket's AC#3 just emptied, which is worth deciding deliberately.

Either way the defect itself is FIXED on main today; what remains is which resolver shape the project wants.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DESIGN ADJUDICATION (independent verification session) — NOTHING CHANGED: no AC ticked, no description edit, no --force, ticket left in_progress. This comment is the only write I made. I was dispatched to close this ticket, verified the collision flagged in the comment above independently, and stopped.

WHAT I RE-VERIFIED FIRST-HAND (measurement, not inference)

1. `compaction_child_repo_root` exists NOWHERE on origin/main @ 25ea12c200ae: `git grep -c compaction_child_repo_root origin/main -- .` exits 1 (no match). The current AC#1/AC#4 therefore describe a symbol that is not in the tree. Confirmed: ticking them would be false. I did not.

2. `_proc.detached_child_cwd` MEASURED, not assumed. Built the real topology — a main checkout with a durable `.tickets-tracker`, an ephemeral `git worktree` whose `.tickets-tracker` is a SYMLINK into it — and called the real helper: it anchors at the durable main checkout, escaping the ephemeral worktree. Source agrees (`_proc.py:141`, `os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(tracker))`, with realpath load-bearing per bugs 3198/93a9).

3. The merged fix's FALLBACK arm, pinned AT THE SEAM. With `REBAR_ROOT` unset, that real symlink store, and the cwd set to the real `detached_child_cwd` anchor, `run_sweep(symlink_tracker)` hands `compact_all_cli` the durable main checkout — not the ephemeral worktree, not `dirname(symlink)`. Mutation-checked: `repo_root=None` and `repo_root=os.path.dirname(tracker)` both FAIL it. Worth noting because the in-repo AC#4 test (`::test_run_sweep_resolves_the_code_root_without_rebar_root`) is end-to-end only and SURVIVES the `repo_root=None` mutant — only `::test_run_sweep_hands_the_resolved_code_root_to_the_sweep` kills it, and that test runs the REBAR_ROOT arm. So the fallback arm's seam pin is real behaviour but is not yet asserted in the repo suite.

4. Full mutant matrix against merged `c68cc1de3185` (each applied then reverted; tree verified clean after):
   - `dirname(tracker)` (re-seed the defect): 3 of 4 run_sweep tests FAIL. Killed.
   - `None`: only the seam test fails. Killed by the seam test alone.
   - `dirname(os.path.realpath(tracker))`: 3 of 4 FAIL. Killed. — see point 6, this one matters.
   Suite green as merged: 51 passed across the three touched modules; `scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` exits 0; the guard self-test is non-vacuous (re-adding a `# repo-root-ok:` marker to compact_trigger.py makes it FAIL).

THE DESIGN QUESTION, ON THE MERITS

The critique of the merged design is legitimate and I confirm its factual basis: `repo_root_or_none()`'s non-`REBAR_ROOT` arm reads git-toplevel-of-CWD, so local correctness depends on `detached_child_cwd` continuing to anchor the child. And `run_sweep` does have a SYNCHRONOUS caller — `maybe_compact` calls `run_sweep(tracker)` inline when `compact.trigger == "always"` (tests/CI) — where no anchoring applies and the cwd is simply the caller's. That is a real non-local coupling and it is uneven.

But two verified facts decide it against the proposed replacement:

5. THE REPLACEMENT'S FALLBACK ARM REGRESSES A CASE THE MERGED CODE GETS RIGHT. `dirname(canonical tracker)` is operationally mutant 3 above, and mutant 3 FAILS `::test_run_sweep_resolves_the_code_root_without_rebar_root` — a relocated store with `REBAR_ROOT` UNSET and the cwd inside the checkout. There, `repo_root_or_none()` resolves the checkout correctly while `dirname(canonical tracker)` yields the external store's parent: the ORIGINAL BUG, reproduced. The proposed design is correct only while `REBAR_ROOT` is exported for every relocated store; the merged one is correct whenever EITHER `REBAR_ROOT` is set OR the cwd is in the checkout — a strictly wider envelope. Note this also answers the synchronous-caller objection in the merged design's favour: in the inline `trigger == "always"` path the caller's cwd is inside the code checkout, which is exactly where git-toplevel is RIGHT and `dirname(canonical tracker)` is WRONG.

6. THE REPLACEMENT WOULD BE INVISIBLE TO THE GATE, NOT MERELY SANCTIONED. I probed `scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` with both forms in one file under `src/`. It flags `os.path.dirname(tracker)` and does NOT flag `os.path.dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)` — the detector matches the bare name `tracker`, a `*.tracker_dir()` call, or those wrapped in `str()`, and deliberately does not unwrap the realpath/abspath family (its own docstring says so; that family is split to flowered-basaltic-beagle). So the proposed fallback would need no `# repo-root-ok:` sanction at all. That is worse than re-populating the allowlist: a composing site of exactly the class this gate exists to catch would sit in the tree unflagged and unsanctioned, while AC#3 truthfully reports "zero deferred config-root sites". The guard's own remedy text names `config.repo_root_or_none()` as a sanctioned fix — the merged code follows the gate's stated guidance.

RECOMMENDATION — disposition (a): ACCEPT WHAT LANDED.

`c68cc1de3185` carries LLM-Review+1 and Verified+1, is merged, drains the last sanctioned site, and has the wider correctness envelope. The stale artefact is the AC text, not the code. Reconcile AC#1 and AC#4 to the merged design (keeping the superseded text visible as a note, so the pivot stays auditable), then tick and close. AC#2a/#2b/#3/#5/#6 already match the tree exactly and are evidenced above; AC#6's culprit is confirmed — `d2dea317ec94` carries `rebar-ticket: 1fde-becd-942a-4351` and introduced the `repo_root = os.path.dirname(tracker)` line, and the `caused_by` link to 1fde-becd-942a-4351 is present with provenance=explicit.

Against disposition (b): landing the resolver as a refactor on top would narrow the correctness envelope (point 5) and reintroduce an undetectable composing construct (point 6). If the cwd coupling is judged unacceptable on its own terms, the right fix is not `dirname(canonical tracker)` but making the child's root explicit without composing it from the store — a separate design ticket, not a change to this one's ACs.

TWO FOLLOW-UPS WORTH FILING (not filed by me; I am not the ticket's owner this session):
  - Seam-pin the fallback arm in the repo suite: `::test_run_sweep_resolves_the_code_root_without_rebar_root` is end-to-end only and survives `repo_root=None`. My verification script above is the shape it should take.
  - Decide whether the guard should unwrap `StorePaths(...).canonical` as a store shape, so a future `dirname(canonical tracker)` cannot enter the tree unflagged (point 6). Possibly belongs to flowered-basaltic-beagle (088b-e4c1-050c-4516).

comments.body:
## STOP + ESCALATION — this bug is ALREADY FIXED and MERGED; my change would REVERT it

While waiting on CI for my Gerrit change 2352, a parallel session working this same ticket posted a heads-up. I verified its claims independently against origin/main. Summary of what I found:

**The fix already landed.** `c68cc1de3185` ("Resolve the sweep's code root, not compose it", Gerrit 2344) is an ancestor of current `origin/main` (`565e1856bc9d`). On origin/main `run_sweep` already reads `repo_root = _cfg.repo_root_or_none()` (line ~233), the `# repo-root-ok:` sanction is already removed, and the four `run_sweep` tests + the guard self-test are already present. It merged with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.

**My worktree base was stale.** This worktree was branched from `ae203145`, which PREDATES the 2344 merge, so the buggy `dirname(tracker)` still appeared here and I implemented against it. The approved-plan premise ("the ONE site auspicial deliberately deferred", unfixed) is no longer true.

**My change (2352) is worse AND would revert the merged fix.** It replaces `repo_root_or_none()` with `compaction_child_repo_root(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)`. Because `main` is Rebase-If-Necessary, submitting it would land that replacement on top of the merge — reverting it. And the operator-approved `dirname(canonical tracker)` fallback is measurably narrower. Hard measurement I ran (relocated store, NO symlink, `REBAR_ROOT` UNSET, cwd inside the checkout — the inline `maybe_compact(trigger="always")` case):

- `dirname(canonical tracker)` → the external store's PARENT (`/…/elsewhere`) = the ORIGINAL BUG.
- `repo_root_or_none()` → the checkout = CORRECT.

The merged design is correct when EITHER `REBAR_ROOT` is set OR cwd is in the checkout; `dirname(canonical tracker)` needs the store to be a symlink co-located with the checkout, a strictly narrower envelope. My in-worktree AC#4 test passed only because it used a co-located SYMLINK store, not this relocated-no-symlink case.

**Actions I took (safe, reversible; no force, no destructive ops):**
- Set Gerrit 2352 to **WIP** so no session can submit it.
- Did **NOT** submit, **NOT** abandon, **NOT** close this ticket.
- Left the earlier description edit in place; note it now mandates `compaction_child_repo_root`, which exists nowhere on origin/main — it reflects the approved-but-now-superseded plan, pending operator direction.

**Why I am escalating rather than proceeding:** resolving this requires a design decision beyond the approved scope — e.g. (a) accept the merged `repo_root_or_none()` design, abandon 2352, and close this ticket against `c68cc1de3185`; or (b) rework 2352 as a refactor ON TOP of the merge if the resolver still wins on evidence (it does not, per the measurement above). Both are operator calls. The approved instruction was to *implement* `dirname(canonical tracker)`; reality diverged.

**Related follow-ups filed by the parallel session (for context):** feisty-intense-mandrill `9058-0b67-4c6a-49c4` (the config-root guard does not flag `dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)`, so that construct would sit unsanctioned); arty-larval-titmouse `a027-d86c-8a00-407c` (the merged in-repo AC#4 test survives the `repo_root=None` mutant, so the fallback arm is currently unasserted).

compiled_state.description:
## Summary (RESOLVED — see resolution note)

SITE: `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py` `run_sweep(tracker)` — the detached-child compaction entry point formerly composed its config root as `repo_root = os.path.dirname(tracker)`, sanctioned `# repo-root-ok:` in the config-root guard (`scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py`) as the ONE deferred CONFIG-ROOT site of the auspicial-friended-merganser class.

CONTEXT: split off from auspicial-friended-merganser (2ec7-be89-9b01-496a), which fixed the 8 clean `dirname(tracker)`-as-config-root sites. `run_sweep` is spawned with cwd == the canonical STORE and inherits only `tracker`; auspicial DEFERRED this site because the detached child needs a DURABLE code root.

IMPACT (milder than the parent's AC#1): on a relocated store (`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` — the deployed MCP topology, store `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, code `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`) `run_sweep` read DEFAULT compaction config (threshold 10, 1800 s horizon) instead of the project's `[compact]` block — folding the right tickets by the WRONG rule. No gate was disabled.

## RESOLUTION — fixed on origin/main by Gerrit 2344 (`c68cc1de3185`)

This bug is FIXED and MERGED. `c68cc1de3185` ("Resolve the sweep's code root, not compose it", Gerrit 2344, carrying `rebar-ticket: 6bf1-326b-7404-4034`) merged with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` and is an ancestor of current `origin/main`.

The landed fix calls the bare `config.repo_root_or_none()` in the child (`compact_trigger.py` `run_sweep`, `repo_root = _cfg.repo_root_or_none()`), and removes the `# repo-root-ok:` sanction. One resolver covers BOTH supported topologies:

- **Deployment** (relocated store): `REBAR_ROOT` is exported unconditionally and names the provisioned checkout `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`, so the `REBAR_ROOT` arm resolves the real code root.
- **Local `make worktree`** (co-located store): the git-toplevel arm reads a cwd that `_proc.detached_child_cwd` has already anchored at the canonical store's parent — the durable main checkout, not the ephemeral worktree. `None` (nothing resolved) passes through as the discover sentinel.

This design has a strictly WIDER correctness envelope than the alternative `dirname(canonical tracker)` fallback once considered here: it is correct when EITHER `REBAR_ROOT` is set OR the cwd is inside the checkout, whereas `dirname(canonical tracker)` regresses the relocated-store + `REBAR_ROOT`-unset + cwd-in-checkout case back to the original bug (measured; see ticket comments). Rejected alternatives in the landed change: threading the resolved root through the spawn contract (re-runs the durability class of bugs 3198/93a9), and `snapshot_repo_root()` (snapshot-only `"."` fallback).
